items.stem: Under the EU AI Act, a CV-screening tool used for hiring is generally treated as:

options.text: A high-risk AI system with specific obligations
options.rationale: Correct: employment-related screening is in the high-risk category.
It is high-risk and regulated, not outright banned.
Hiring use is not minimal risk.

options.text: Out of scope because it uses a spreadsheet
options.rationale: Tooling format does not remove it from scope.

items.explanation: Correct: employment-related screening is in the high-risk category.

items.stem: Which TWO obligations typically apply to high-risk AI systems? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Human oversight of the system's use
options.rationale: Correct: high-risk systems require meaningful human oversight.
Correct: documentation and logs are required.
No such guarantee is required or possible.
The opposite: high-risk systems face scrutiny.

items.explanation: Correct: high-risk systems require meaningful human oversight.

items.stem: Why does the Act's extraterritorial reach matter to a US-only company?

options.text: It can apply when the system's output is used in the EU market
options.rationale: Correct: placing a system or its output on the EU market brings it in scope.

options.text: It never applies outside the EU
options.rationale: It can apply based on EU market use.
It applies to AI systems broadly.

options.text: It applies only to open-source code
options.rationale: Scope is not limited to open source.
